issues.legal_issue: A permanent structure built on leased land qualifies as being for residential or business purposes when it is adapted to those uses, whether or not the tenant built it for personal use.
material_facts: The tenant was contractually entitled to build on the leased land and built permanent structures within the prescribed five-year period.
The structures included buildings for residential use and warehouses adapted for business use.
The tenant let out buildings constructed on the land.
issues.conclusion: The statutory requirement is satisfied by a permanent structure adapted for residential or business purposes; the tenant need not have built it for personal use.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(1)(a) of the Non-agricultural Urban Areas Tenancy Act, 1955, the first statutory route to protection requires that the tenant be entitled under the tenancy contract to build, actually build a permanent structure within five years of the contract, and build a structure adapted for residential or business purposes. The Court rejected adding a requirement that the tenant use the structure personally. It noted that the Act had retrospective operation under Refiquennessa v. Lal Bahadur Chetri & Others.

predicates.landlord_eviction_case: A landlord has brought a proceeding seeking to evict a tenant from leased land.
predicates.tenant_entitled_to_build: The tenancy contract entitled the tenant to build on the leased land.
predicates.permanent_structure_built_within_five_ye: The tenant built a permanent structure on the leased land within five years of the tenancy contract.
predicates.structure_adapted_for_residential_or_bus: The permanent structure was adapted for residential or business use, regardless of whether the tenant intended to use it personally.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks to evict a tenant who was entitled to build and built a qualifying permanent structure within the specified period, the tenant is protected from eviction except for rent default.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant of land does not lose statutory protection from eviction merely by letting out qualifying structures built on the land.
material_facts: The tenant held the land under a tenancy and qualified for protection because he was entitled to build and had built permanent structures adapted for residential or business use within the prescribed period.
The tenant let out the structures to others but continued to possess the land as its tenant.
The landlords sought vacant possession of the land.
issues.conclusion: Letting out the structures does not cause the tenant of the land to forfeit the statutory protection; the landlord-tenant relationship concerning the land continues until lawfully determined.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(1)(a) of the Non-agricultural Urban Areas Tenancy Act, 1955 confers protection on the tenant of the land, not on tenants of buildings constructed on it. A building adapted for residential or business use does not cease to have that character when let out. The Court did not decide whether a sub-tenant of the land could independently claim protection under section 5(1)(a) by virtue of the definition of “tenant” in section 3(g).

rule.if: landlord_eviction_case and tenant_entitled_to_build and permanent_structure_built_within_five_years and structure_adapted_for_residential_or_business_use and tenant_let_out_structures

predicates.landlord_eviction_case: A landlord has brought a proceeding seeking to evict the tenant of the land.
predicates.tenant_entitled_to_build: The tenancy contract entitled the tenant to build on the leased land.
predicates.permanent_structure_built_within_five_ye: The tenant built a permanent structure on the leased land within five years of the tenancy contract.
predicates.structure_adapted_for_residential_or_bus: The permanent structure was adapted for residential or business use.
predicates.tenant_let_out_structures: The tenant let out to others structures built on the leased land while remaining the tenant of the land.

issues.definition: When a tenant who built a qualifying structure lets it out while remaining the tenant of the land, the letting does not forfeit the tenant's protection from eviction.
